nodes.label: Assignments (set tag)
nodes.rationale: Variables set inside blocks/loops do not leak out (if statements excepted); namespace objects are the sanctioned way to propagate changes across scopes.

nodes.label: Block Assignments (set ... endset)
nodes.rationale: Provides multi-line strings since Jinja does not support triple quotes.

nodes.label: HTML Escaping
nodes.rationale: Default is no autoescaping because escaping known-safe values (numbers, booleans) is a performance hit and safety information is fragile, risking double-escaping.

nodes.label: with Statement
nodes.rationale: Since 2.9, variables in the with opening statement refer to outer scope, cleaning up earlier unintended cross-references; now enabled by default without an extension.

nodes.label: Macros
nodes.rationale: Reusable function-like idioms (DRY); underscore-prefixed macros are private; child-template macros do not override parent macros due to scoping.

nodes.label: Template File Extension (.jinja)
nodes.rationale: Any extension works; .jinja helps IDEs but autoescape-by-extension must account for the extra suffix.

nodes.label: BaseLoader
nodes.rationale: All loaders subclass BaseLoader; custom loaders override get_source. Compiled modules cached in a size-limited cache with auto reload.

nodes.label: block Tag
nodes.rationale: Duplicate block names in one template are disallowed because a block works in both directions: placeholder and content for the parent.

nodes.label: Scoped Blocks
nodes.rationale: Blocks cannot see outer-scope variables by default because a child template replacing the block would reference variables not defined in it; 'scoped' opts in.

nodes.label: Template Inheritance
nodes.rationale: Described as the most powerful part of Jinja: a base skeleton template defines blocks that child templates override.

nodes.label: for Loop
nodes.rationale: for-else runs when no iteration happened (not on no-break as in Python) since Jinja loops cannot break by default.

nodes.label: Loop Filtering
nodes.rationale: Substitute for break/continue; the loop variable counts only iterated items.

nodes.label: Attribute vs Subscript Lookup (getattr / __getitem__)
nodes.rationale: foo.bar tries getattr first then __getitem__; foo['bar'] tries item first then attribute; matters when an object has both an item and attribute of the same name.

nodes.label: namespace
nodes.rationale: Allows carrying a value from within a loop body to an outer scope, working around set-scoping rules.

nodes.label: Special loop Variable (index, cycle, depth, previtem, changed)
nodes.norm_label: special loop variable (index, cycle, depth, previtem, changed)

nodes.label: Import Context Behavior (with/without context)
nodes.rationale: Includes get the current context, imports do not, because imports are cached and used as macro modules; adding with context disables caching.

nodes.label: i18n trans Block
nodes.rationale: trimmed modifier avoids hard-to-read, error-prone translation strings caused by whitespace/linebreaks; keyword args to format because languages reorder words.

nodes.label: Bug report issue template
nodes.rationale: Tracker is only for bugs in Jinja itself; requires minimal reproducible example, full traceback, Python and Jinja versions.

nodes.label: Feature request issue template
nodes.rationale: Asks whether the problem is solvable without changes to Jinja, e.g. by subclassing or using an extension.

nodes.label: Highlighting Active Menu Items
nodes.rationale: Assignments outside blocks in child templates are global and run before the layout, so the child can set active_page.

nodes.label: BytecodeCache
nodes.rationale: Stores generated bytecode externally to avoid parsing templates on first use, helping apps that compile many templates on the first request.

nodes.label: Environment
nodes.rationale: Central object storing configuration and globals; most apps create one at init, multiple side by side only when configurations differ.

nodes.label: PackageLoader
nodes.rationale: Simplest way to configure loading: only requires the package be importable, resolves the templates folder path automatically.

nodes.label: NativeEnvironment
nodes.rationale: Renders to native Python types instead of strings, useful when Jinja is used outside text generation.

nodes.label: Pylons
nodes.rationale: Recommends setting pylons.strict_c so missing attributes yield undefined objects rather than empty strings.

nodes.label: Switching from Mako
nodes.rationale: Jinja has no embedded Python code; move logic to pre-render processing or globals/filters.

nodes.label: Global Namespace
nodes.rationale: Environment.globals for data common to all templates, Template.globals for per-template data; globals must not change after loading because they may be shared.

nodes.label: How fast is Jinja
nodes.rationale: Compiles templates to Python code and caches them by name plus bytecode cache; benchmarks discouraged as they don't reflect real use.

nodes.label: Jinja Templating Engine
nodes.rationale: Application logic belongs in Python, but the designer's job should not be made difficult by restricting functionality too much.

nodes.label: Async Support
nodes.rationale: Disabled by default; enabling compiles different code with await wrappers around all calls, adding overhead vs pure async code but transparent to template designers.

nodes.label: Autoescaping
nodes.rationale: Built-in since 2.9 but not enabled by default; users are encouraged to configure it explicitly because the default may change for security reasons.

nodes.label: Why HTML Escaping Is Not the Default
nodes.norm_label: why html escaping is not the default
nodes.rationale: Jinja is general purpose (text, LaTeX, CSS, JS...), and autoescaping adds compile/render overhead even with MarkupSafe C speedups.

nodes.label: Logic in Templates
nodes.rationale: Some logic is needed for expressiveness; Jinja forbids arbitrary Python to keep engine maintainable and templates readable.

nodes.label: Null-Default Fallback
nodes.rationale: Exploits dynamic inheritance: extends inside an if only applies when standalone is false.

nodes.label: StrictUndefined
nodes.rationale: Closest to regular Python behavior: disallows all operations except testing for undefined.

nodes.label: Undefined
nodes.rationale: Implemented by overriding dunder methods; subclasses customize which operations fail via _fail_with_undefined_error.

nodes.label: SandboxedEnvironment
nodes.rationale: Renders untrusted templates by intercepting attribute access, method calls, operators, mutation, and string formatting.

nodes.label: Operator Intercepting
nodes.rationale: Operators are compiled directly for performance, so interception requires intercepted_binops/unops to make the compiler emit call_binop/call_unop calls.

nodes.label: Sandbox Security Considerations
nodes.rationale: Sandbox alone is not perfect security: catch errors, limit CPU/memory, postprocess output, and pass only relevant data.

nodes.label: Autoescape Extension (jinja2.ext.autoescape)
nodes.rationale: Removed and made built-in in 2.9; enabling it does nothing.

nodes.label: With Statement Extension (jinja2.ext.with_)
nodes.rationale: Built-in since 2.9; extension is a no-op.

nodes.label: AST Nodes (jinja2.nodes.Node)
nodes.rationale: AST may change between versions but stays backwards compatible; compiler converts nodes to Python code objects.

nodes.label: Jinja Extensions
nodes.rationale: Move often-used code into reusable classes (e.g. i18n); extensions can add filters, tests, globals, or extend the parser.

nodes.label: Writing Extensions
nodes.rationale: Non-trivial; the compiler does not validate the node tree, so malformed ASTs cause hard-to-debug errors.

nodes.rationale: Imports may_break from subbroken.html and calls it in a loop to demonstrate an error raised inside an imported macro.

nodes.label: may_break macro
nodes.rationale: Divides item by zero to deliberately raise ZeroDivisionError from within a macro.

nodes.label: mojibake.txt fixture (non-ASCII text)
nodes.rationale: Contains Japanese text for testing template file encoding handling.

nodes.label: Async mode (enable_async)
nodes.rationale: Added in 2.9 for Python 3.6 async iterators; since 3.0 no longer patches Jinja itself; sync render of async templates uses asyncio.run.

nodes.label: MarkupSafe dependency
nodes.rationale: Builtin markup class removed in 2.5.1 in favor of markupsafe; Markup/escape must be imported from MarkupSafe since 3.1.

nodes.label: NativeEnvironment / NativeTemplate
nodes.rationale: Renders templates to native Python types instead of strings.

nodes.label: PackageLoader
nodes.rationale: Uses PEP 451 API since 3.0; earlier attempt to drop setuptools/pkg_resources was reverted in 2.11.2 due to Pytest issues and Python 2 support difficulty.

nodes.label: pass_context / pass_eval_context / pass_environment decorators
nodes.rationale: Unified, renamed replacements for contextfunction/contextfilter, evalcontextfunction/evalcontextfilter, environmentfunction/environmentfilter (deprecated in 3.0, removed in 3.1).

nodes.label: SandboxedEnvironment
nodes.rationale: Repeated security fixes (str.format, str.format_map, |attr, clear/pop on mutable sequences, operator intercepting) to prevent code execution and information leakage from untrusted templates.

nodes.label: Template traceback rewriting
nodes.rationale: Tracebacks show correct template line numbers and hide internal compiler frames.

nodes.label: xmlattr filter
nodes.rationale: Disallows keys with spaces, /, >, = for security (GHSA advisories); user input should never be used as keys.

nodes.label: Exceptions point to correct template line
nodes.norm_label: exceptions point to correct template line

nodes.label: HTML autoescaping
nodes.rationale: Prevents XSS from untrusted user input.

nodes.label: JIT/AOT compilation to optimized Python code
nodes.norm_label: jit/aot compilation to optimized python code

nodes.label: Sandboxed environment
nodes.rationale: Safely render untrusted templates.

nodes.label: Pull request template
nodes.rationale: Requires a linked ticket, tests that fail without the change, docs updates, a CHANGES.rst entry, and versionchanged markers.

nodes.label: Version 2.11.0
nodes.rationale: Last version to support Python 2.7/3.5; adds ChainableUndefined, debug extension, better tracebacks, NativeTemplate fixes.

nodes.label: Version 2.9 (codename Derivation)
nodes.rationale: Introduces async mode, policies, scoping-system overhaul so include/import propagate context consistently, built-in with/autoescape tags.

nodes.label: Version 3.0.0
nodes.rationale: Drops Python 2.7/3.5, adds type hints, PEP 451 PackageLoader, required blocks, unified pass_* decorators, async no longer requires self-patching.

nodes.label: Version 3.1.0
nodes.rationale: Removes previously deprecated code: WithExtension/AutoEscapeExtension built in, context*/evalcontext*/environment* decorators replaced by pass_* decorators, Markup/escape must come from MarkupSafe.

nodes.label: Version 3.1.5
nodes.rationale: Sandbox handles indirect str.format calls, escapes template names in error messages, async generator cleanup (aclose), FileSystemLoader error lists searched paths.

nodes.label: Version 3.1.6
nodes.rationale: Security fix: |attr filter no longer bypasses environment attribute lookup so the sandbox can apply its checks (GHSA cpwx-vrp4-4pq7).

nodes.label: Version 3.2.0 (Unreleased)
nodes.rationale: Drops Python 3.7-3.9, raises MarkupSafe>=3.0 and Babel>=2.17, deprecates __version__ in favor of importlib.metadata/feature detection, moves to pyproject.toml metadata with flit_core build backend instead of setuptools/setup.cfg.

nodes.label: Scoping system overhaul (2.9)
nodes.rationale: Made scoping consistent with designer/developer expectations; no magic difference between include and import constructs, context always propagated the same way.

nodes.label: Jinja design philosophy
nodes.rationale: Application logic belongs in Python where possible, but templates should not restrict functionality so much that the designer's job becomes difficult.

nodes.label: Context (jinja2.runtime.Context)
nodes.rationale: Immutable; for performance Jinja uses the context only as a primary data source, not as storage. Functions should return values to assign rather than mutate it.

nodes.label: EvalContext (Evaluation Context)
nodes.rationale: autoescape should be checked on the eval context rather than the environment because it holds the computed value for the current template; must only be modified via EvalContextModifier nodes from extensions.

nodes.label: Low Level API
nodes.rationale: Fragile; exposed for debugging and advanced extension techniques, not recommended for general use.

nodes.label: Identifier Naming Rules
nodes.rationale: Filters and tests live in separate namespaces and may contain dots to group by topic.

nodes.label: Literals (strings, numbers, lists, tuples, dicts, booleans)
nodes.norm_label: literals (strings, numbers, lists, tuples, dicts, booleans)

nodes.label: Math Operators
nodes.rationale: Chained ** evaluates left-to-right unlike Python; extended math should be done in Python before render.

nodes.label: Babel Integration (jinja2.ext.babel_extract)
nodes.rationale: Template syntax errors are ignored by default on the assumption that tests catch them; set silent = false to change.

nodes.label: Policies
nodes.rationale: Environment-level knobs (truncate.leeway, urlize.rel, json.dumps_function, ext.i18n.trimmed, etc.) that tweak filter/runtime behavior, usually security related.

nodes.label: New Style Gettext
nodes.rationale: Less typing, less error prone, better autoescaping: formatting is part of the call, only named placeholders are allowed, and translated strings are marked safe.
